author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts health officials reported the state's seventh human case of West Nile virus this year on Friday, according to NBC 10. The patient is a man in his 60s who was exposed in Worcester County.

The Department of Public Health continues to classify West Nile risk as moderate across much of Massachusetts. Risk is listed as high in Boston, Brookline, Cambridge, Chelsea, Everett, Malden, Newton, Revere, Somerville, Watertown and Winthrop. Officials have identified 307 mosquito samples carrying the virus in 13 counties, including Bristol County. Eastern equine encephalitis has also been detected in mosquitoes this season.

West Nile is usually spread through the bite of an infected mosquito. Many infected people develop no symptoms, but severe illness can occur, especially among older adults and people with weakened immune systems. Health officials recommend using an EPA-registered repellent, wearing long sleeves and pants when practical, repairing window screens and removing standing water around homes. Residents should also consider limiting outdoor activity from dusk to dawn, when many mosquitoes are most active.
dek: State health officials say a man in his 60s was exposed in Worcester County as mosquito-borne disease risk remains elevated across much of Massachusetts.
headline: Massachusetts reports seventh human West Nile case of 2026
